content: iOS Safari introduces an AudioContext state value beyond the spec's suspended/running/closed: 'interrupted', entered automatically when the user leaves the page (switches tabs, minimizes Safari, locks the screen). Returning to the page does not auto-resume it — the app must explicitly call audioCtx.resume() again, typically from a visibilitychange handler, or audio stays dead. Desktop Chrome generally auto-suspends/auto-resumes AudioContext on tab hide/show without requiring this, but explicit resume-on-visible is the safe cross-browser pattern (MDN BaseAudioContext.state, AudioContext.resume()).
